Matthew Perry, the beloved actor best known for his role as Chandler Bing on "Friends," died on October 28, 2023, at the age of 54. He was found unresponsive in the pool of his Pacific Palisades home and was pronounced dead at the scene. Cause of DeathAn autopsy report released in December 2023 determined that Perry died from the "acute effects of ketamine," with contributing factors of drowning, coronary artery disease, and buprenorphine (used to treat opioid addiction). While Perry had been undergoing legal ketamine infusion therapy for anxiety and depression, the high concentration of the drug in his system at the time of his death indicated he had sought unsupervised, illicit doses. Criminal Investigation and SentencingFive people were charged in August 2024 in connection with supplying the lethal doses of ketamine to Perry. All five individuals entered guilty pleas. Jasveen Sangha ("The Ketamine Queen"): Identified as the dealer who supplied the ketamine, Sangha was sentenced on April 8, 2026, to 15 years in federal prison. Dr. Salvador Plasencia ("Dr. P"): A physician who sold ketamine to Perry in the weeks before his death, he was sentenced in December 2025 to 30 months in prison. Kenneth Iwamasa: Perry's live-in assistant who injected him with the lethal doses, pleaded guilty and is awaiting sentencing. Erik Fleming: An intermediary who sold the ketamine to Iwamasa, is scheduled to be sentenced in June 2026. Dr. Mark Chavez: A physician who sold ketamine to Plasencia, was sentenced in December 2025 to eight months of home detention and three years of supervised release. Legacy and BackgroundThroughout his life, Perry was open about his long, public battle with drug and alcohol addiction. He wrote about these struggles in his 2022 memoir, "Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing". Following his death, the Matthew Perry Foundation was established to support people struggling with addiction.
